speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the newborn has bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance. When did these symptoms first begin, and has the baby passed any meconium stools since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the infant passed any meconium stools since birth, and is there any visible distension of the abdomen? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The abdominal X-ray demonstrates a 'double bubble' sign, which is indicative of duodenal atresia. Physical examination confirms distension of the upper abdomen with a concave lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: The 'double bubble' sign on the X-ray is classic for duodenal atresia, which explains the bilious vomiting and upper abdominal distension. Given this clear radiographic evidence and clinical presentation, I am confident in my diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia
